version.reason: The EVM target is what decides whether the grace-period name is reserved, so iterating targets shows both sides of the Cancun boundary.

expected_solc_divergence.reason: solc 0.8.36 declines the Frontier target outright ('Invalid EVM version requested'), which counts as a rejection, while slang accepts the declaration.

Before Cancun solc accepts `let mcopy := 1` with only a warning ('mcopy' will be promoted to a Yul reserved identifier in the future; plus a deprecated-EVM warning on the oldest targets), which counts as a rejection. slang correctly accepts the grace-period name until the built-in exists, so the statuses differ until warnings are distinguished from errors.
